# Pixel Veil

> A free Chrome extension for front-end developers: lay a design image over the live page you built, and see every pixel that disagrees.

Pixel Veil puts a design export (a Figma frame as a PNG, a screenshot, any image) on top of a web page, so
the page can be checked against its design. It is free, open source under MIT, and needs no account.

## What it does

- Any number of image layers per site, each with its own position, see-through level and scale.
- Four ways to compare, including Difference, where matching pixels turn black.
- Line a layer up by dragging, with arrow keys, or with Center and Fit width.
- Groups, layers pinned to the window, Chrome's side panel, and export and import of a site's layers.

## Privacy

- At install it can read no site. Clicking its icon lets it draw on that one tab.
- "Keep on this site" asks Chrome for that one site, so layers come back after a reload.
- Images and settings stay in the browser. It sends nothing anywhere.

## Limits

- Images: PNG, JPEG, WebP and GIF, up to 25 MB each.
- Layers are kept per site, not per page.
- Not on the Chrome Web Store yet: download a release, or build it from source. Firefox 140+ builds and passes
  Mozilla's linter but has not been run in Firefox.

- [The page](https://ank-khoaho.github.io/pixel-overlay/): what it is, in one screen
- [The guide](https://ank-khoaho.github.io/pixel-overlay/guide/): install it, then every control, step by step
- [Compare a design](https://ank-khoaho.github.io/pixel-overlay/guide/compare.html): add a design, line it up, blend modes
- [Organise your layers](https://ank-khoaho.github.io/pixel-overlay/guide/organise.html): groups, pinned layers, keep on a site, export and import, side panel
- [Keyboard](https://ank-khoaho.github.io/pixel-overlay/guide/keyboard.html): every shortcut
- [Privacy and permissions](https://ank-khoaho.github.io/pixel-overlay/guide/privacy.html): what it can read, step by step
- [Limits and questions](https://ank-khoaho.github.io/pixel-overlay/guide/reference.html): limits, what was tried, answers
- [The README](https://github.com/Ank-KhoaHo/pixel-overlay#readme): how to install and use it, its limits and its alternatives

- [The source](https://github.com/Ank-KhoaHo/pixel-overlay): the code and its MIT licence
